summary: Burlington, CT summit lookout: 50-ft steel tower erected on land Harry Ney gave the state in 1929 (opened 1930 per Wikipedia); no longer standing; no source describes remains at the summit.

facts.status_note: Wikipedia says it is no longer standing; Forest Lookouts lists it as removed, with no date. Summit now has a quail barn and a radio tower per Wikipedia; sources do not say what remains of the lookout.
facts.agency: Connecticut State Park and Forest Commission

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. Wikipedia says the blue-blazed Tunxis Trail traverses the mountain.

events.note: Harry Ney, the owner, said he would build and equip a lookout station on the mountain (1924 publication quoted by Forest Lookouts); planned, not yet built
In spring 1929 Harry Ney gave the state a plot on the summit; a 50-foot steel tower was erected there (state report quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Wikipedia says the tower opened in 1930 after land was donated by Harry Ney; this differs from the 1929 erection date

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1929 state report quoted by Forest Lookouts says the tower was erected in spring 1929; Wikipedia says it opened in 1930. Build year recorded as 1929 with the 1930 opening noted.
Wikipedia names Paul S. Ney as an early owner in the early 1900s; the 1924 and 1929 quotes name Harry Ney. Sources do not explain how they relate.

sources.title: Johnny Cake Mountain - Forest Lookouts (quoting 1924 and 1929 state reports)

notes_for_editor: Build year conflicts: 1929 state report (erected spring 1929) vs Wikipedia (opened 1930). The Wikipedia citation for the 1930 date (footnote 8 on that page) was not confirmed. Owner naming differs (Paul S. Ney vs Harry Ney). The summit 'radio tower' is listed by Wikipedia among summit features and separately a WJMJ broadcast tower sits below the summit; neither is tied to the 1929 site. Public access to the summit is not established in any source read, so no access level is recorded. The FFLOS registration date from the brief was not verified. The 2016 town purchase is recorded from Wikipedia, which itself says it needs citations.
